spec.title: Separated local agent and authenticated web channels

status.comment: Owner selected a password-protected Quicklens web gateway on the agent computer behind an HTTPS tunnel. Public deployment is separate from implementation and local acceptance.

p.channel-separation: Agent MCP adapters, the durable broker and the ZAP application communicate through their local interfaces. Their listeners remain bound to loopback. Internet access terminates at a separate Quicklens web gateway exposing only named UI operations. It provides neither an arbitrary forwarding target nor a general ZAP, MCP, shell or agent command endpoint. The gateway and local clients reuse the shared lens model and domain services inside org.vibevm.zap/lens.

p.deployment-profile: The web gateway runs on the same computer as ZAP and the agents. An explicitly configured HTTPS tunnel forwards only the web gateway. The gateway itself may bind loopback behind that tunnel; its configured public origin must use HTTPS. Tunnel and proxy trust is explicit. Untrusted forwarded headers cannot enable a secure profile, select a destination or identify a user. Local browser pairing and Electron remain separate supported profiles. Configuring this profile does not install a tunnel, publish a hostname or change firewall rules.

p.password-authentication: The web profile requires password authentication before exposing plan data or UI actions. Password-verifier and access configuration may live under the current user's ~/.vibe/zap directory. Store a salted slow password hash using a supported cryptographic implementation, with bounded verification cost and concurrency; do not retain the plaintext password. Setup and rotation avoid command-line secrets and logs. Authentication attempts are bounded and throttled. A missing verifier or invalid secure configuration refuses startup rather than enabling anonymous access.

p.web-sessions: Successful authentication creates a cryptographically random, expiring, revocable server-side session. HTTPS session cookies use Secure, HttpOnly and an explicit SameSite policy. Logout and password rotation invalidate applicable sessions. The page and every data, action and invalidation endpoint enforce authentication. State-changing requests bind the session's CSRF protection and exact permitted origin. The password is accepted only by the dedicated HTTPS login flow. Authentication tokens and passwords are not placed in URLs, localStorage, plan or broker-message payloads, or renderer configuration.

p.web-authority: Web authentication establishes the configured human UI scope; it does not create agent identity, ZAP coordinator authority or Owner approval. The trusted local service retains backend credentials. Existing distinctions between viewing, answering questions, proposing changes and recording an exact required Owner decision remain enforced. A remote answer cannot approve another operation, and an agent adapter never receives the human web password, session or Owner credential.

p.managed-terminal-extension: PROP-006 adds optional terminal observation and input-control operations for registered Lens-owned managed sessions. These are separately configured and authorized UI capabilities with project/session/control-epoch binding; ordinary web login, viewing or chat does not grant terminal input. They may use the authenticated UI gateway without exposing a raw PTY host listener, arbitrary executable or general shell/proxy route. Native-only deployments retain the original interface without requiring this module.

p.verification: Local acceptance uses isolated synthetic credentials and a local HTTPS proxy fixture. It verifies successful login and permitted UI operations, refusal of anonymous access, wrong passwords, tampered or expired sessions, logged-out sessions, wrong origins and missing CSRF protection. Raw agent/backend routes remain unavailable through the web gateway. Tests confirm local listeners, bounded authentication work, credential-free renderer data and preservation of local browser/Electron behavior. Such evidence does not claim that a public tunnel has been deployed.
